input.quote: (a) At any time that there is no uncompleted Statement of Work outstanding, either party may terminate this Agreement for any or no reason upon fifteen (15) days advance notice to the other.
input.rationale: Section 6 gives a convenience right only "[a]t any time that there is no uncompleted Statement of Work outstanding," so while any Statement of Work is in flight neither party — including us — may terminate without cause; the only other exit (6(b)) requires an uncured material breach. Because the term is evergreen (Section 2: continues until terminated under Paragraph 6) and Statements of Work are the operative vehicle for all Services, we effectively have no convenience right for engagements running well beyond 12 months. That fails both the preferred position (Customer convenience on 30 days' notice with pro-rata refund) and the fallback (60–90 days' notice), and sits in walk-away territory. We therefore propose a new Section 6(c) giving Company a 30-day convenience right over the Agreement and any Statement of Work, with Contractor paid only for Services performed, prepaid fees refunded, and work in progress assigned. The Contractor-side 15-day convenience right in 6(a) is tolerable as drafted because it can only be exercised when no Statement of Work is outstanding (i.e., no active engagement to abandon), so we have not disturbed it.

ops.text: (c) In addition, Company may terminate this Agreement or any Statement of Work for convenience, in whole or in part and for any or no reason, upon thirty (30) days advance written notice to Contractor, without penalty, early-termination charge or forfeiture of any amounts. Upon any such termination, Contractor will be paid all fees and expenses incurred or earned for Services properly performed through the effective date of such termination, Contractor shall refund to Company any prepaid fees for the period after such effective date, and Contractor shall provide to Company, and hereby assigns to Company, all right, title and interest to any Works in progress.

proposal.comment: [Playbook] We have added a Company right to terminate this Agreement or any Statement of Work for convenience on 30 days' notice, because Section 6(a) permits convenience termination only when no Statement of Work is outstanding, leaving us locked into in-flight engagements under an indefinite term. Our playbook requires a customer convenience right on 30 days' notice with no early-termination penalty and a refund of prepaid fees; we can discuss 60 days' notice as a fallback.
proposal.summary: Add Company termination-for-convenience right on 30 days' notice covering outstanding Statements of Work, with no penalty and refund of prepaid fees.
